aiAnalyses.testName: › chromium › ui/dedup-demo.spec.js › Dedup Demo › broken selector always fails — dedup demo @regression
aiAnalyses.summary: The test 'broken selector always fails — dedup demo' intentionally uses a non-existent CSS selector '#this-element-does-not-exist' and asserts it is visible, causing a guaranteed failure. The element is never present in the DOM, so the locator times out after 3000ms.
aiAnalyses.likelyRootCause: The test is deliberately written with a broken/invalid selector ('#this-element-does-not-exist') as a demonstration or deduplication test case. The selector does not correspond to any real DOM element, making the toBeVisible() assertion impossible to satisfy. This appears to be an intentional 'always-fail' test used to demonstrate deduplication behavior in the reporter, not an accidental regression.
aiAnalyses.suggestedRemediation: If this test is intentionally broken for demo/dedup purposes, it should be tagged with test.fail() or test.skip() to signal the expected failure state and prevent it from polluting CI results. If it was meant to test a real element, replace '#this-element-does-not-exist' with the correct, stable selector for the target element. If it is purely a reporter demonstration fixture, consider moving it to a dedicated fixtures directory and excluding it from regression runs via tag filtering or project configuration.

structuredFeedback.reasoning: The selector '#this-element-does-not-exist' is a placeholder/intentionally invalid selector. It will never resolve to a DOM element in any environment. The test name itself ('broken selector always fails') confirms this is by design. The fix depends on intent: mark as expected failure with test.fail() for demo purposes, or replace with a real selector if this was meant to validate an actual UI element. The @regression tag makes this particularly problematic as it will always fail in CI pipelines.
